bars:Istioploikos.name: Istioploikos
bars:Istioploikos.teaser: A two-level deck at the tip of Mikrolimano, the sailboats moored right under the rail
bars:Istioploikos.story: Mikrolimano was Mounichia, one of the war harbours of Themistocles' Athens; today its curved quay holds the yacht basin, and Istioploikos, 'the yachtsman', has held its tip since 1997. It stands a little apart from the row of fish terraces, a two-deck building that looks like a small liner about to cast off. The café side runs from the morning; the bar and kitchen take over late, and a DJ plays on Sunday afternoons. As the light goes, the ouzo turns cloudy over ice and a whole grilled tsipoura or fangri comes to the rail, the masts knocking below.
bars:Istioploikos.why: Come for the sundowner on the upper deck, not for a cheap round: you pay for the position.
facts: The tip of the Mikrolimano quay, apart from the fish-terrace row
Ouzo over ice, then a whole grilled fish off the kitchen
Sunset on the upper deck; Sunday afternoon for the DJ

bars:Horizon Rooftop of Senses.name: Horizon Rooftop of Senses
bars:Horizon Rooftop of Senses.teaser: Three staggered decks over Mikrolimano's caiques, built to feel like standing on a ship
bars:Horizon Rooftop of Senses.story: A hundred metres along the same quay, at Akti Koumoundourou 24, Horizon opened around 2022. The designer Stratos Chiotellis built it as a ship's superstructure: metal arches, wooden decking and three levels set at different heights, so each one frames the basin from a new angle and the marina stands in for a fourth wall (LiFO, May 2026). The day starts with brunch at weekends, poached eggs on sando bread, pancakes, a club sandwich, and ends with cocktails as the caiques' lights come on. People come for the deck and the sunset more than for the mixing.
bars:Horizon Rooftop of Senses.why: Climb to the top level before sunset; the lower decks lose the open sea behind the masts.
facts: Akti Koumoundourou 24, Mikrolimano, above the fishing caiques
A golden-hour cocktail; weekend brunch by day
The hour before sunset; open about 10:00 to 02:00 (seen Jul 2026)

bars:801 Rooftop Bar.name: 801 Rooftop Bar
bars:801 Rooftop Bar.teaser: Eight floors up, level with the cranes and the night ferries of the Great Harbour
bars:801 Rooftop Bar.story: Spyros Metaxa built his first distillery in Piraeus in 1888, and the brandy was made in the port until 1968, when the company moved to Kifissia. Converting the waterfront building into the Mitsis N'U hotel in 2024, Divercity Architects kept the shapes of the barrels in wooden arches and amber light. The 801 is on the eighth floor at Aristidou 16–20, opposite Gate E7, and you drink eye-level with the gantries as the night boats back out for the islands. The list leans Greek: Liminality builds reposado tequila and Metaxa 12 with chamomile, mustard seed and pink grapefruit.
bars:801 Rooftop Bar.why: This is the commercial port at full scale, the opposite of Mikrolimano: watch a ferry leave from up here.
facts: Mitsis N'U Piraeus Port, Aristidou 16–20, opposite Gate E7, 8th floor
Liminality, or the Auteur's Colada: pandan, tsipouro, rum and coconut under Prosecco
Evening departures; seasonal, late April to October, 18:00 to 01:30 (Oct 2026), shut in winter

bars:Hams & Clams.name: Hams & Clams
bars:Hams & Clams.teaser: French oysters opened to order and a low-intervention glass on the Zea Marina deck
bars:Hams & Clams.story: It began in 2016 in a 50 m² room and later moved onto the deck at Zea Marina, where Pasalimani's calm inner basin and moored yachts feel a world away from the ferry gates. The oysters come from France and are opened as you order, with a Bloody Mary oyster shot to start; the rest of the list runs to clam linguine, spicy tuna tartare, jamón ibérico and culatello cut thin. It is listed on Raisin, the natural-wine app, but the growers by the glass are not published, so ask what is open tonight. A raw bar at marina prices, not a deep natural cellar.
bars:Hams & Clams.why: Start with the Bloody Mary oyster shot, then ask the floor which natural bottle is open.
facts: Whatever natural white is open, with French oysters
Early evening on the deck as the marina lights come on

bars:Paléo.name: Paléo
bars:Paléo.teaser: Two to three hundred obscure southern-European labels in a Retsina-quarter warehouse
bars:Paléo.story: The quarter is called Retsina, the port's old tobacco-warehouse grid, inland and with no view, and Paléo fills one of those warehouses at Polydeukous 39. The sommelier-owner Yannis Kaimenakis travels the south of Europe for small wineries few people have heard of, two to three hundred labels in all, and prices them close to retail on principle, which in a port of marina markups is a stand. The by-the-glass list can change daily. Let him choose, and order pasta e fagioli or the Tuscan chicken-liver pâté to keep the bottle company.
bars:Paléo.why: Say what you like and let Kaimenakis pour; the point is a grower you will not find elsewhere.
facts: Polydeukous 39, Retsina quarter; an industrial street, no sea
The glass of the day, chosen at the counter
Opening time, 18:30, Monday to Saturday; closed Sunday (seen Jul 2026)

bars:Méthe.name: Méthe
bars:Méthe.teaser: Forty labels reaching Austria and Georgia, and 48-hour pizza, on the ferry avenue
bars:Méthe.story: Méthe is the Greek word for wine's euphoric drunkenness, and the bar that took the name opened on 2 January 2026 at Akti Miaouli 73, facing the blue-domed church of Agios Nikolaos, patron of sailors. In the open kitchen the chef Levis Kodimai works a wood-fired oven: Neapolitan pizza from a 48-hour dough, Black Angus tartare with burnt-leek mayonnaise, handmade rooster ravioli, a small cheese board with house jams. The list is forty labels with eleven by the glass, and it travels, Austria and Georgia among them. Akti Miaouli is a working port avenue, not a view.
bars:Méthe.why: Order the 48-hour pizza and whatever Georgian or Austrian glass is open.
facts: Akti Miaouli 73, opposite the church of Agios Nikolaos
One of the eleven by the glass, from Austria or Georgia
Dinner after the ferries have loaded

bars:Amsterdam Bar.name: Amsterdam Bar
bars:Amsterdam Bar.teaser: Bowie on the wall, bicycle-saddle stools on the marina pavement, drinks until 05:00 at weekends
bars:Amsterdam Bar.story: Dimitris Doumakis opened the place in 2008 as O'Canto, then renamed it Amsterdam to bring a piece of the Dutch capital to Pasalimani. Inside there is Muppet Show memorabilia and a painting of Bowie; outside, stools made from bicycle saddles line the Akti Moutsopoulou pavement facing Zea Marina, and the speakers run from pop to metal. The pour is plain and honest: the house Zombie, a classic Margarita, whisky by the glass, cold draught. One drinker alone or a whole crew both fit, it gets loud at weekends, and there is no kitchen.
bars:Amsterdam Bar.why: The late stop after a marina dinner, when everything else on the bay has closed.
facts: Akti Moutsopoulou, Pasalimani, facing Zea Marina
The house Zombie or a classic Margarita; draught beer
After midnight on a Friday or Saturday; open daily 10:00 to 03:00, to 05:00 at weekends (seen Jul 2026)

bars:The Art of Bragi.name: The Art of Bragi
bars:The Art of Bragi.teaser: A small cocktail room on the Piraiki, the sea breeze through the open windows
bars:The Art of Bragi.story: Nikoletta Biza has run this bar at Akti Themistokleous 154 since December 2009, out on the Piraiki, the western peninsula where the coast stays rocky and nobody has built a marina. She named it for Bragi, the Norse god of poetry, and each drink comes with its history: the White Zombie pours white and agricole rum over Fassionola cordial, Caribbean pineapple and velvet falernum. Jazz, funk, soul and blues on the speakers, a whisky shelf for neat drinkers, the windows thrown open to the sea air. Snacks only, no kitchen.
bars:The Art of Bragi.why: Ask Biza for the story behind the drink; the menu is written to be told.
facts: Akti Themistokleous 154, on the Piraiki coast road
The White Zombie, or a neat whisky
A warm night with the windows open

bars:Retsina — the port's wine.name: Retsina — the port's wine
bars:Retsina — the port's wine.teaser: Savatiano with Aleppo-pine resin in the ferment: the white the port has drunk with fried fish for a century
bars:Retsina — the port's wine.story: Retsina is the one wine here that can claim to be local. It is mostly Savatiano, sometimes with a splash of Roditis, and Aleppo-pine resin goes into the must while it ferments, which gives the pine note. It is not a PDO but a traditional appellation, an OKP, belonging to the Mesogeia plain east of Athens, close enough for the port to call it its own; its vineyards belong to the Athens guide. In Piraeus it comes cold, in a tin jug or a short bottle, beside the fried fish. The barrel version poured in Agios Dionysios has its own card in the tables: To Eidikon.
bars:Retsina — the port's wine.why: Drink it very cold with something fried and salty; that is the job it was made for.
facts: Pale gold and cold, pine over a dry, lightly bitter white
The word Retsina and the traditional-appellation mention; Mesogeia (Ρετσίνα Μεσογείων) for the local one
Retsina from the barrel (apo to vareli) where there is one, otherwise a cold bottle with the fish

bars:Ouzo with the fried fish.name: Ouzo with the fried fish
bars:Ouzo with the fried fish.teaser: Anise that turns milk-white on ice, a karafaki at a time, and the small fried fish that slow it down
bars:Ouzo with the fried fish.story: At the ouzeri the drink is the point and the food comes to keep you there. Ouzo is an anise-flavoured grape spirit; drop in ice or water and it clouds white, the louche, as the anise oils come out of solution. Its geographical indication is reserved to Greece and Cyprus, and its home is Plomari on Lesvos, not this quay. Tsipouro is the rougher cousin, distilled from the skins and stems left after pressing, usually without anise; in Crete the same idea is tsikoudia, called raki. Neither was born here. Both are what the port pours, with fried gavros, lemon and a few mezedes.
bars:Ouzo with the fried fish.why: Order a karafaki, add ice yourself, and wait for the fish: ouzo is drunk with food, never alone.
facts: Clear until the ice goes in, then milk-white, anise on the nose
Ouzo, often with Plomari or Lesvos; tsipouro with or without anise
A karafaki of ouzo or tsipouro, ice on the side, and a plate of fried gavros

listening:Rebetiko was born here.name: Rebetiko was born here
listening:Rebetiko was born here.teaser: The Greek urban blues took its classic shape on these docks after 1922
listening:Rebetiko was born here.story: Rebetiko, the Greek urban blues, took its classic bouzouki-led shape in working-class Piraeus in the 1920s and 30s, in the tekedes, the hashish dens, of Drapetsona, Agios Dionysios and the Lemonadika fruit market by Karaiskaki Square, as refugees from the 1922 Asia Minor catastrophe crowded the port. The bouzouki and the baglamas came ashore on the same quays as the ouzo and the meze. Under the Metaxas regime, in power from August 1936, the songs were censored and the hashish lyrics cut. The music survived. UNESCO inscribed rebetiko on its intangible-heritage list in December 2017.
listening:Rebetiko was born here.why: Hear it in a room in the quarters it came from, not in a show staged for a tour bus.
facts: Propolemikon in Agios Dionysios, where the old quartet played, and Revaizi on the Drapetsona edge; both are in this guide
Athens and Piraeus both claim the cradle, and the Smyrna café style and the Piraeus bouzouki style are told as rival roots; the UNESCO entry speaks of urban working-class people, not of one quarter

listening:The Famous Quartet of Piraeus.name: The Famous Quartet of Piraeus — 1934
listening:The Famous Quartet of Piraeus.teaser: Four players, two bouzoukis, a baglamas and a voice: the first band of its kind
listening:The Famous Quartet of Piraeus.story: In 1934 Markos Vamvakaris, Giorgos Batis, Anestis Delias and Stratos Pagioumtzis began playing together as «Η τετράς η ξακουστή του Πειραιώς», the Famous Quartet of Piraeus: two bouzoukis, a baglamas and singing, the first group made of bouzouki and baglamas specialists. Batis gave it the grand name; he had run his own café in the port since 1931. None of the four was born in Piraeus. In 1935 they recorded «Φραγκοσυριανή» (Frangosyriani) together. The Metaxas regime's censorship broke the run within a few years.
listening:The Famous Quartet of Piraeus.why: Put on a 1930s recording of the four before you go to a rebetadiko; you will hear where every band since comes from.
facts: Propolemikon in Agios Dionysios, which keeps the quartet in its house history; its own card is in the tables
Where they first played: in.gr says the Anastasi at Konstantopoulos's place, Ta Nea a room at Sarantopoulos's in Drapetsona, and Propolemikon claims them too

listening:Bayanteras — the one rebetis b.name: Bayanteras — a son of the port
listening:Bayanteras — the one rebetis b.teaser: He came from Piraeus itself, and gave his own back-street quarter a song
listening:Bayanteras — the one rebetis b.story: Dimitris Gogos, known as Bayanteras (1903–1985), was born in Piraeus on 28 February 1903, in the working-class quarter of Hatzikyriakio. That sets him apart: the founding quartet were islanders and refugees who came ashore, and none was a native. He became one of rebetiko's most influential singers and composers. The nickname is tied to Kálmán's operetta Die Bajadere, which by the usual account he arranged for bouzouki around 1925. In 1938 he wrote «Χατζηκυριάκειο», putting the name of his home quarter into the songbook.
listening:Bayanteras — the one rebetis b.why: Walk Hatzikyriakio with «Χατζηκυριάκειο» in your ears; the song is about the streets around you.
facts: Hatzikyriakio, the quarter he was born in and wrote his 1938 song about
How he got the nickname: the Bajadere arrangement story is the usual account, not a documented fact

listening:Revaizi.name: Revaizi
listening:Revaizi.teaser: A live kompania three nights a week, on the ground where the tekedes stood
listening:Revaizi.story: Revaizi, at Thermopylon 28 on the Drapetsona side of the port, is a mezedopoleio with bouzouki in the quarter where the hashish dens once stood. A full kompania plays Friday, Saturday and Sunday, and the regulars sing along. The kitchen is Cretan rather than Asia Minor: chochlioi, snails fried with rosemary, a risotto with apaki, the smoked Cretan pork, and raki in small bottles. Come as much for the room and the raki as for the set list. It is out toward Drapetsona, a taxi ride rather than a walk from the cruise gates.
listening:Revaizi.why: Book a table for a Saturday and order the snails with the first carafe of raki.
facts: Thermopylon 28, Drapetsona edge; a taxi from the cruise gates
Live music Friday, Saturday and Sunday (seen Jul 2026); ring before you go
Chochlioi with rosemary, apaki risotto, raki

listening:Stou Thoma & To Palio Roloi.name: Stou Thoma & To Palio Roloi
listening:Stou Thoma & To Palio Roloi.teaser: Two central rooms where the regulars, not a tour group, get up to dance the zeibekiko
listening:Stou Thoma & To Palio Roloi.story: Two rooms in the town centre keep live rebetiko away from the waterfront. Stou Thoma, at Mavromichali 22–24 in Agia Sofia, sits in an arcade that was once the ticket entrance of an open-air cinema; the kompania plays Wednesday to Saturday from about ten at night. To Palio Roloi, at Dimosthenous 5 beside the covered market, is in old Troumba, the sailors' quarter of Never on Sunday, and its band starts on Friday and Saturday afternoons around five, when the regulars get up for the zeibekiko. Both change their hours.
listening:Stou Thoma & To Palio Roloi.why: Go to Palio Roloi for a weekend afternoon, Stou Thoma for a late weekday night.
facts: Stou Thoma: Mavromichali 22–24, Agia Sofia. To Palio Roloi: Dimosthenous 5, by the covered market
Stou Thoma Wed–Sat from about 22:00; Palio Roloi Fri–Sat from about 17:00 (seen Jul 2026); ring first
Meze and a carafe, and let the night run

listening:Kafeniote.name: Kafeniote
listening:Kafeniote.teaser: A wood-panelled evening kafeneio on the Kastella slope, live rembetika on Sunday night
listening:Kafeniote.story: Uphill on Leoforos Vasileos Georgiou B' toward Kastella, at the corner of Mouson, Kafeniote is a new kafeneio-ouzeri in the old style that opens only in the evening. The owner makes his own raki; the meze runs to smoked grey mullet under wood panelling and low lamplight. On Sunday night the room turns over to live rembetika, and the seats go early. It is not a daytime café or a place to work: it is a warm room for after dark.
listening:Kafeniote.why: Arrive early on Sunday for a seat before the musicians start.
facts: Leof. Vasileos Georgiou B' at Mouson, on the slope up to Kastella
Wed–Thu 17:00–01:30, Fri–Sun 17:00–02:00, closed Mon–Tue; live music Sunday night (seen Jul 2026)
The owner's raki and the smoked mullet; EUR 5–10 a head (seen Jul 2026)
No: evenings only, and no laptop tables

listening:Ta Paidia tou Pirea — 1960.name: 'Ta Paidia tou Pirea' — 1960
listening:Ta Paidia tou Pirea — 1960.teaser: A song about the boys of Piraeus, shot on these quays, won an Oscar in 1961
listening:Ta Paidia tou Pirea — 1960.story: «Τα Παιδιά του Πειραιά», music by Manos Hadjidakis, sung by Melina Mercouri as Ilya in Jules Dassin's «Ποτέ την Κυριακή», Never on Sunday, was set and filmed in the port in 1960. On 17 April 1961 it won the Academy Award for Best Original Song, the first winner in a language other than English. Hadjidakis stayed away from the ceremony. The tune went round the world in English with words by Billy Towne, which were not the ones heard in the film. The Greek lyric never mentions Sunday; the title was the film's.
listening:Ta Paidia tou Pirea — 1960.why: Watch the film before you come, then walk the Troumba streets and the quays it was shot on.
facts: Old Troumba, the sailors' quarter of the film, around To Palio Roloi; the song is still requested in the rebetiko rooms
Some at the time claimed Hadjidakis took the melody from a folk tune; why he skipped the ceremony is told differently from source to source

listening:Hi-fi — honestly.name: Hi-fi — honestly
listening:Hi-fi — honestly.teaser: No hi-fi listening bar in Piraeus this guide can vouch for; the real listening here has no speakers
listening:Hi-fi — honestly.story: A listening bar is a room where the sound system and the records are the point and the drinks come second. An October 2026 search found none in Piraeus confirmed by a venue or the quality press, so none is listed here. The port's listening is older and louder: a kompania of bouzouki, guitar and baglamas playing to a room that knows the words, often with little or no amplification. If you want to hear rebetiko properly, sit near the musicians in one of the rooms in this fold. For a vinyl room, the Athens guide has one.
listening:Hi-fi — honestly.why: Choose a seat close to the bouzouki rather than looking for a sound system.
facts: The live rooms in this fold: Revaizi, Stou Thoma, To Palio Roloi and Kafeniote
